My advice: section-level placement is a defensible bounded relaxation of presentation, not necessarily a semantic change. I would test it rather than insist that renderer-owned type/caveat remain visible at every scroll position. But describe the relaxation explicitly: unchanged author content does not mean unchanged access to qualifications.

Established basis: the September 9 section-rhythm consultation at @session:default/run_4ee2883ee9a14bca94e717104b156585 explicitly preserved persistent qualifications, and my advice then discouraged separating the caveat merely to clean up the top. That was a constraint of that review and my design recommendation—not evidence of a permanent PO mandate requiring every renderer caveat to remain sticky. The subsequent review at @session:default/run_0e49c82d29454ff09843e625dd4dc955 retained that arrangement. Your newly reported PO feedback supports reconsidering the header, but does not approve this particular remedy.

Why I favor this experiment: title, breathing room, then provenance/scope gives the header a clearer hierarchy. Moving “Procedure · not execution status” or “Chronology · not causation” onto the existing sequence landmark places the interpretation beside the structure it explains. That is more purposeful than another competing header line, while retaining the accepted section boundaries and connected scan.

The important limit is mid-scroll interpretation. Discovery and offscreen author text preserve availability, not immediate visibility. Persistent “not executed” already helps the supplied procedure example; a chronology may lack an equivalent persistent warning against reading connectors as causal. Inspect both cases mid-sequence—not only their improved tops. If the visible fragment positively suggests execution or causation without the section label, the move is insufficient for that case. Otherwise I would not add redundant sticky text preemptively.

One concrete mechanical risk: the previous review’s measurement/render equivalence depended on a short, single-row landmark. A labeled rule is longer. Confirm it fits supported widths without clipping the negation, introducing extra rows, or breaking heading/first-item attachment and paging. “Same row count” remains a proposed invariant, not something established by the description.

So: reasonable mechanics-owned comparison, explicitly revising the earlier persistence choice while preserving meaning and author qualifications. PO acceptance remains unresolved: does the quieter header improve the screenshot experience without making scrolled content misleading? I have not seen this screenshot, inspected the new implementation, or verified its behavior.
